result:
Decision: **CONTINUE.** Round 267 fixes GATE264-S2 (Medium): on Windows AltGr keyboards, typing ż, ę, ł or ą (outside a text field) ran Undo, Split, Loop or Duplicate. The planning files are written and the store is untouched (HEAD `7ba7cd2`, clean tree).

**Round 266 result.** C passed it with browser evidence at both viewports. The split changed no audio sample in the WAV exports. Gate 266 published rounds 265–266 as `7ba7cd2`, which is the baseline for round 267.
- SABA-B-11c stage 1 is done.
- C-R265-01, C-R265-02 and B-R264-RANGE-HOW-COPY are closed.
- C's only finding, C-R266-01 (Low), was a defect in my own grep in the task, not in the code. I closed it as a planning finding and made it a candidate lesson for the next retro.

**Why GATE264-S2 now.** The previous planning had already set it as the next bug round, and the 3-day regression round isn't due until 2026-11-02. I reproduced it again on `7ba7cd2` in Chromium at both viewports:
- AltGr+Z undoes, AltGr+E splits, AltGr+D duplicates and AltGr+L reaches the loop handler.
- A plain Ctrl+Alt+Z also undoes.

**The fix.** In the Studio keydown handler, a Ctrl/Cmd+letter shortcut fires only when neither Alt nor AltGr is held.
- It covers the ten letter shortcuts (Z, Y, E, L, A, D, C, X, V, G) and the "edit blocked during drag" message.
- Ctrl+Alt+O (Overview), Space, the zoom keys and the plain-letter keys are unchanged.
- The Live 12 manual (ch. 42) treats Ctrl+Alt+letter as different commands from Ctrl+letter, so this matches Live. The manual says nothing about AltGr, so C will mark those rows "unconfirmed".
- A may edit three files: `StudioWorkspace.tsx` (that handler only), `meta-shortcuts-ui.test.tsx` (add-only, rows AG1–AG6) and a new doc 199.
- A also has to show 14 targeted changes to the fix each turning a named test red, so the new tests are known to catch a regression.

**My pre-check on a scratch copy with the fix applied.**
- Tests: 24 Alt-related test files pass (507/507) and 40 Ctrl/Meta test files pass (725/725). TypeScript compiles. No existing test conflicts with the fix.
- Browser, both viewports: every Alt and AltGr chord now does nothing. Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Shift+Z, Ctrl+E, Ctrl+L and Ctrl+Alt+O still work.

**New from the gate-266 review.**
- **GATE266-S1 (Medium)**, a regression from stage 1: when a time selection extends past the selected clip, the details panel shows only the part inside the clip, and pressing Enter shrinks the selection to the clip. The evidence so far is the reviewer's reading of the code. I'll reproduce it in the browser before round 268, which will fix it together with two related Low wording issues ("both edges" when only one edge was cut, and "Clips split" when one part wasn't cut).
- Three Lows went to the deferred polish list, now 443 entries.

**For root.** `StudioWorkspace.tsx` has now been edited three rounds running, so I wrote a non-blocking addendum to the existing architecture checkpoint request (`b-round-266-checkpoint-addendum.md`). One unverified idea (AltGr on Linux might still trigger single-letter keys like M) is on the Tech Lead list and is not scheduled.

**Advisor.** It was configured but overloaded on my first call and couldn't be used this turn, so I planned from the browser repro, the scratch pre-check and the manual.

**Not COMPLETE** because the two open Mediums, SABA-B-11c stage 2 and SABA-B-7 (both waiting on Saba), SYS-5/6, performance, the store redesign, later queue entries and the deferred Lows remain. **Not BLOCKED**: round 267 needs no credentials or approval.
